item.title: UAE, Bahrain Jointly Dispatch Urgent 100 Tonnes Of Aid To Gaza Strip
item.description: In cooperation with ‘’Operation Chivalrous Knight 3’’ and the Emirates Red Crescent of the United Arab Emirates, the Royal Humanitarian Foundation of the Kingdom of Bahrain (RHF) has dispatched an urgent 100-tonne relief shipment to the Gaza Strip on the occasion of the holy month of Ramadan. The aid was sent via Al-Arish Airport in Egypt in preparation for its entry through the Rafah Border Crossing. item.title: Oman Reviews Children’s Social Media Use Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: Oman is considering a new framework to regulate children’s use of social media, as authorities respond to growing concerns over digital safety and the impact of online platforms on young users. The Telecommunications Regulatory Authority has begun a comprehensive review of how children engage with social networking sites, after studies highlighted potential risks ranging from excessive screen time to exposure to harmful or inappropriate content. item.title: Kuwait Plans Freelance Visa To Curb Residency Trade And Reform Labour Market
item.description: Kuwait is moving towards introducing a regulated freelance visa, as part of an effort to overhaul its labour market and curb the long-standing trade in residency permits. The proposal, announced by First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Interior Sheikh Fahd Al Yousef during a recent meeting with private sector representatives, would allow expatriates to work independently without a traditional sponsor, under a structured and legally supervised framework. item.description: The High Criminal Court set March 31 to issue its verdict in a case involving a defendant accused of causing the death of one person and injuring three others in a traffic accident. item.title: Bahrain: Bounced Cheques Can Now Be Enforced Without Court Case
item.description: Holders of dishonoured cheques can now move straight to enforcement through the national portal, without filing a court claim, under a new decision issued by the Ministry of Justice. Decision No. 6 of 2026 regulates the enforcement of cheques returned unpaid and allows them to be executed directly through the “ Execution Services” on bahrain.bh. The cheque is treated as an enforceable instrument under amendments to the Commercial Law, removing the need to begin proceedings before the civil court

item.title: Bahrain: Jail And BD10,000 Fine In Deepfake Proposal
item.description: Up to BD10,000 and jail could face anyone who produces or falsifies audio or video under a proposed new deepfake offence, due for debate in the Shura Council on Sunday despite a committee call for the measure to be rejected. item.title: Bahrain: Court Jails Expat Worker For BD4,633 Embezzlement
item.description: A Filipina expat who handled petty cash at a catering business has been sentenced to six months’ imprisonment after a court found she took BD4,633 by cycling company withdrawals through staff bank accounts and back to herself via a money transfer app. The Lower Criminal Court also ordered her to repay the money, ruled the sentence should be carried out, and said she is to be deported after serving her term. item.title: Bahrain: Public Fasting Violations May Lead To Jail Or BD100 Fine
item.description: The Public Prosecution in the Kingdom of Bahrain has reiterated that publicly breaking the fast during the holy month of Ramadan is a punishable offence under the law. item.title: Bahrain: Social Insurance For Self-Employed Workers
item.description: A proposal to bring freelancers and other self-employed workers under mandatory social insurance won unanimous approval in Parliament. The measure amends Article (2) of the Social Insurance Law issued by Decree-Law No. 24 of 1976, widening compulsory cover beyond workers on employment contracts to include self-employed people and members of the liberal professions.
